rites.name: Veonaulanum
rites.text: A rhyming call that a wanderer teaches to travelers, to be chanted when they are in peril so the chanter comes to their aid. When a cold grave-spirit threatens companions, the chant summons a rescuer who drives the spirit away into daylight.

rites.name: Serilus Amirum
rites.text: A word-root of the old speaking folk that means to grasp a thing fully and make it clear within the mind. Elders use it when teaching the young to see past surfaces.

rites.name: Riarneolium
rites.text: A woodland call sung by a wandering spirit of the glens to rouse the sleeping hollows at dawn. It is one of the many songs the spirit chants as he roams the land.

rites.name: Amilasia
rites.text: A chilling chant sung by a burial-mound dweller that traps travelers within its tomb. It starts as a faint murmur and grows into a bone-deep freezing incantation.

rites.name: Reonaurium
rites.text: A chanted incantation that a single wanderer sings over a blade to sharpen it. Its verses hold strange notions found nowhere else in the lore, and the chant is later forgotten.

rites.name: Neorium
rites.text: A chanting rhyme sung by a forest wanderer to drive away a restless burial spirit. The words call on the daylight to force the undead creature from its tomb.

rites.name: Veleostes
rites.text: A word-root from an ancient tongue that carries the sense of forming a warm bond with another. It is used to describe both friendship and deep affection.

rites.name: Cantor Sines
rites.text: A chant composed by an ancient northern bard, marking the start of a seafaring journey. It was later gathered into a collection of scholarly songs.

rites.name: Ceoneles
rites.text: A rhyming marching song performed by a wandering forest dweller to guide small travelers along a winding reed-lined stream. The melody is completed together by two residents when the travelers arrive at their dwelling.

rites.name: Cianum
rites.text: A slow walking-song sung by a tree-herder while carrying two travelers through an ancient wood. It is chanted after a spell of silence, recalling a time when the forests spread far wider.

rites.name: Amaunium
rites.text: A chanted incantation makes a captive's tresses grow long, and the locks are woven into a dark cloak carrying a drowsing enchantment.

rites.name: Seronastia
rites.text: A word-root meaning to bring forth offspring. Its past-form is a related form, and it has a near-equivalent that shares its meaning.

rites.name: Veornastus
rites.text: An ancient spoken chant kept by a forest folk that names every living creature they know. It is recited aloud by an elder, and its full length is thought to exceed what is spoken.

rites.name: Serantor Orarnines
rites.text: A small, precise motion of the hand, named for the digits that perform it. It means to grasp or pluck something lightly with the fingertips.

rites.name: Corernanum
rites.text: A word in an elder tongue that names a flame which springs upward in leaps. Scholars of old speech trace it to a refined dialect spoken by the fair folk.

rites.name: Viarnor
rites.text: A word-root that names the act of swift leaping or dashing on foot, used by living creatures that run with their legs and not by flowing liquids.

rites.name: Valonasium Leolaurnium
rites.text: A tactile sensing practice in which a person sweeps an open palm across a surface to learn its texture. The gesture is simply a way of feeling things with the hand.

rites.name: Sereornium Visterus
rites.text: A verb of tender touch between two lips, used in the speech of the old court. Some scholars argue a lengthened form of it may also be spoken in the newer tongue.

rites.name: Viantaulia
rites.text: A stilling root in an invented tongue, meaning to halt into stillness. Its descendant forms were later deleted by a scholar who revised the lexicon.

rites.name: Rantanum Silium
rites.text: A word-root that means to gaze upon something, to keep sight of it, or to stand guard over it. Its meanings shift between simply observing and actively watching over.

rites.name: Telauseria
rites.text: A dread force wielded by tyrant lords to frighten free folk into submission. It can be a feared idea that lures people to depend on a dark master, or a literal shadow that spreads over lands.

rites.name: Taurnelor
rites.text: A spoken root that signifies a binding ill-wish laid upon another. Its opposite root carries the sense of blessing and goodwill.

rites.name: Corisia
rites.text: A sung verse of measured lines is directed toward a celestial keeper of starlight. Many altered versions of the chant exist, some mixing in words from common trade tongues.

rites.name: Tilliarnium
rites.text: A warrior chants a rising verse of defiance as dawn breaks, singing of charging through doubt and despair toward a fiery reckoning and bloody ruin.

rites.name: Raulonanum
rites.text: A ritual chant that a sailor sings while ferrying hidden travelers past watchful guards across a dark lake. It accompanies a secret crossing into a waterside town.

rites.name: Sirium
rites.text: A solemn ritual observed by a sea-descended people to honor a drowned homeland. Participants stand motionless in quiet remembrance, speaking no words for the lost realm.

rites.name: Lolestia
rites.text: A sacred chant that the people of a hidden valley sing to their guardian spirits. Some believe its verses long for a distant shore beyond the waves.

rites.name: Amornus
rites.text: A devotional verse spoken as a sacred petition, rendered in a hushed tongue of the high temples. Its final two lines remain unfinished, left for worshippers to complete in their own words.

rites.name: Caurniantus
rites.text: A reverent greeting that is spoken only toward revered beings and holy figures. In sacred songs, it is the word used to salute the divine.

rites.name: Corinium Tenintum
rites.text: A word-spoken exchange in which two speakers trade their thoughts back and forth. It is held as a formal practice among the learned orders of the valley.

rites.name: Nernia
rites.text: A stirring war chant that a sovereign calls to his mounted warriors, awakening them and rousing them before a fierce charge into battle.

rites.name: Telonor
rites.text: A root of shaped utterance that gives rise to words for the clever speaker and the eloquent being. It marks the ability to give voice to thought in a fluent, careful way.

rites.name: Raullus
rites.text: A dark craft of spellwork practiced by those who bend hidden forces toward gloom. Its practitioners are feared as the sorcerers of shadowed arts.

rites.name: Mauntum
rites.text: A coined term for the act of searching closely and bringing hidden truths into the open. Scholars of this invented tongue use it to describe careful inspection.

rites.name: Valosus
rites.text: A sacred practice of questioning and examining a matter closely. Scholars use it to mean enquiring carefully into something before drawing conclusions about it.

rites.name: Serares Seriarnia
rites.text: A drive held within the mind that pushes a person toward a chosen goal. It is described as a deliberate intent or a contrived means of bringing about a result.

rites.name: Orolenor
rites.text: A short spoken term that names fire and is commonly taken as a command to kindle a blaze. Scholars of the old tongues note its form as an urging word.

rites.name: Veosilia
rites.text: A devotional chant of praise is rendered into an elegant tongue of the wise, its opening verses honoring the threefold divine and the first five sacred names of a revered mother figure. The work was left unfinished.

rites.name: Meliastanum
rites.text: A grammatical prefix that intensifies the meaning of a word, marking it as very or extremely. It works by multiplying or increasing the sense of the root it attaches to.

rites.name: Telasium
rites.text: A pure radiance from an ancient blessed land that joins skillful craft with sound judgment and grace. Those who learn it from its wise keepers carry it onward and make other peoples more noble.

rites.name: Raulus Cosus
rites.text: A spoken term that appears in an old hymn-like ballad, believed to express the act of raising one's voice in song. It hints at an unrecorded word meaning to sing.

rites.name: Calonus
rites.text: A ceremonial chant composed by two makers and performed when a new sovereign is crowned. It marks the moment a wandering leader takes the throne.

rites.name: Tania Toleosia
rites.text: A root-word of the old tongue that carries the sense of dominion, command, and triumph. It describes the act of mastering others and holding power over them.

rites.name: Oreolum
rites.text: A three-tongued hymn of supplication addressed to a star-queen of the heavens, unfinished and never set down in a published book. It was once recited at a gathering of scholars and shares its shape with devotional songs to a gentle mother-goddess.

rites.name: Vanteollum
rites.text: A word of the old speech meaning to rise, raise, or lift up. Its past tense shifts form depending on whether something is lifted by another or rises on its own.

rites.name: Ceolaurnia
rites.text: A sacred craft of altering the true shape of things through deceit, wearing false forms like masks. Scribes of the temple orders teach it as a discipline of concealment.

rites.name: Corastor
rites.text: An old rhyme of healers' plant-lore that names a herb able to cure a sickness of dark air. Some scholars dismiss it as folk nonsense, yet its words hold a measure of truth.

rites.name: Nestaulles
rites.text: A devotional prayer spoken in an ancient tongue, offered to a distant father who dwells beyond the sky. Several versions circulate, so no single wording is official.

rites.name: Miriantia
rites.text: A ritual verb describing two people bound together as spouses. In older speech, a different word carried that meaning, while this one once meant to dare.

rites.name: Telorestus
rites.text: A word in an old tongue meaning radiance, a bright glow or shine. Related forms appear in neighboring speech, showing how the same idea changes across peoples.

rites.name: Miantus
rites.text: A gift of seeing ahead that is granted to chosen folk of ancient lineage. It appears in varying strength, sometimes surfacing in dreams and visions that guide hard decisions.

rites.name: Velor
rites.text: A hidden quality that people with limited understanding name strangeness, while wise folk see it as part of the everyday world, present but out of sight. Some who look through special sight can glimpse its full radiance beneath ordinary appearances.

rites.name: Lauses
rites.text: A radiant elven sorceress who appears as a playing card within a collectible strategy set of wizards. She is a fabled lady of the woodland realm whose presence bolsters allied characters.

rites.name: Canes
rites.text: A cursed injury made by the blades of a dark master's chief hunters. The enchantment slowly drains the victim, sometimes leaving lasting agony or threatening to turn the wounded into a pale ghost.

rites.name: Roses
rites.text: A word in an elder tongue that stands for the mind, the imagination, and the act of conceiving an idea.

rites.name: Coranteoses
rites.text: A reasoning being's innermost self, the seat of reason and deliberate purpose. It shapes deliberate journeys and resolve, letting a mind choose which chances fate offers.

rites.name: Orialora
rites.text: Orialora is the concept of walls held against the outer dark in Veneruamora's Walled Age, a principle that shaped the orders and churches who keep the sealed ramparts standing. Its adherents describe it as the patience that turns a barrier into a home, and their first crossings through the gates are counted as its greatest deeds.

rites.name: Xaeziathora
rites.text: Xaeziathora is a concept of the Arcane Realm of Veneruamora, a binding of walls and wardens that holds the world's old boundaries in place. In the Walled Age it is remembered as the principle that lets orders and churches keep their first crossings open against the wild groves.

rites.name: Teontanum
rites.text: A melodic composition is performed as a tune for a pairing of two lovers. It stands apart from the usual themes, having been crafted by a different hand than the rest.

rites.name: Tisus Orausor
rites.text: A learned volume that gathers and expands a long-revised treatise on storytelling of wonder, explaining how its author understood the making of invented myths and enchanted tales.

rites.name: Siluannys
rites.text: Siluannys is a sundering pact-fire that was kindled in the Arcane realm during the sixth era, when the bells of a drowned citadel rang in reverse. Its flame gathers the grief of abandoned oaths and then releases it in one vast burst across the sky of Veneruamora. Scholars still argue whether it was lit to defend the realm or to close a door forever.

rites.name: Silaemiel
rites.text: Silaemiel is a sky-scorching rite of the Arcane realm's sixth era, in which a fleet of sworn vessels is set alight by a single oath-kindled flame that burns the bridges between shores. Its ruin is felt as a crimson dawn on the far horizon, and those left stranded upon the coast never forget the sight.

rites.name: Venaemae
rites.text: Venaemae is a silver-throated convergence event in Veneruamora's Arcane realm, when the sky-rivers of the E6 era briefly fold back on themselves and drag the stars into a choir. Scholars of the Lantern Orders record it as a pulse that can wake sleeping mountains and unmake the memories of anyone who hears its final note.

rites.name: Orianeth
rites.text: Orianeth was a gathering of starlit loom-singers that bound the drifting ash of Veneruamora into a single bright lattice over the Sable Reaches. For five years it held, until a tide of unseen hunger climbed its strands and unravelled every singer who stood within its span.

rites.name: Ryarliel
rites.text: Ryarliel is a veil of unbroken dusk that a sorcerous tyrant draws across the sky to blind his foes and sow confusion among their armies. It lasts for days, swallowing the sun over whole kingdoms until the arrival of a late-coming host breaks the gloom and restores hope to the beleaguered peoples below.

rites.name: Veneirwen
rites.text: Veneirwen is the shadow-king of the Arcane realm of Veneruamora, a fallen warden who once bound stars into chains and now dims whole constellations to feed his grip on memory. Scholars of the Sixth Era record that his last great working unmade a sunlit archipelago in a single night, leaving only glass where its cities had been.

rites.name: Mianna
rites.text: Mianna is a ruinous hex-weaver of the Veneruamora's third cycle, whose binding rites once drained a frozen moon of its tides. Her signature working, a grey lattice of hollowed wills, can unmake a settlement's memory of itself and leave only drifting husks behind. Scholars still argue whether she was a tyrant or a desperate mourner who never stopped counting her losses.

rites.name: Alaelys
rites.text: Alaelys is a veiled current of arcane force woven through the cold stone reaches of Veneruamora, appearing as hushed chants that bind rivers to their courses and sigils that wake when spoken aloud. Its practitioners learn to read the world's grain and redirect it, though the greatest workings draw deep upon the old ember-seas beneath the mountains.

rites.name: Ryenniel
rites.text: Ryenniel is an arcane concept in the Veneruamora of the E6 era, a hunger woven into hoarded relics that slowly bends the minds of those who touch them. Its power lies less in fire than in the way it reshapes desire, turning ordinary keepers into possessive guardians of forgotten wealth. Scholars of the age measure its influence in the quiet collapse of entire courts.

rites.name: Nuenioma
rites.text: Nuenioma is an invented arcane script of the Veneruamora, inked in pale silver that only surfaces when a particular lunar phase touches the page. Its keepers taught that a message could lie hidden for ages until the right sky opened it to the reader.

rites.name: Silioneth
rites.text: Silioneth is a sealing-hymn that binds the ruins of a broken mirror-realm, woven from a single choir of remembered silence. When its last verse is sung, the choir's echo folds the enemy's marching banners into the stone beneath them.

rites.name: Karathurnok
rites.text: Karathurnok is a concept of Veneruamora that gives shape to the moment a single future is chosen from the many branching paths of the Three Futures. It is most often felt in the groves and young kingdoms of the first sovereign's age, where its presence steadies choices that might otherwise scatter.
